'''Lewis Edward Kay''', {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|CC|FRS|FRSC}} (born September 26, 1961) is a Canadian academic and biochemist known for his research in biochemistry and [[nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy]] for the studies of the structure and behaviour of proteins.<ref name="Gairdner">{{Cite web|url=https://gairdner.org/2017-canada-gairdner-laureates-announced/|title=2017 Canada Gairdner Laureates Announced!|date=March 28, 2017}}</ref> He is a professor of molecular genetics, biochemistry and chemistry at the [[University of Toronto]] and Senior Scientist in Molecular Medicine at [[The Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto|The Hospital for Sick Children]].<ref name="UofTBio">{{Cite web|url=http://biochemistry.utoronto.ca/person/lewis-e-kay/|title=Lewis E. Kay}}</ref>

==Biography==
Kay received a BSc in biochemistry from the [[University of Alberta]] in 1983, a PhD in molecular biophysics from [[Yale University]] in 1988, and did post-doctoral studies at the [[National Institutes of Health]] under the supervision of [[Ad Bax]].<ref name="UofTBio"/> In 2020, he was honoured as an international member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020|title=2020 NAS Election|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kay is married to biophysicist [[Julie Forman-Kay]], who studies intrinsically disordered proteins.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SBGrid Consortium - Member Tale - Julie Forman-Kay - The Hospital for Sick Children, University of Toronto|url=https://sbgrid.org/members/tale/from-disorder-function|access-date=2021-05-08|website=sbgrid.org}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==

* 1996 – Merck Frosst Award <ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 1998 – Canada's "Top 40 under 40" <ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 1999 – [[Steacie Prize]] for Natural Sciences <ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2002 – Founders Medal International Society of Magnetic Resonance in Biological Systems <ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2002 – [[Flavelle Medal]], [[Royal Society of Canada]]<ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2004 – [[Günther Laukien Prize]]<ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2006 – Elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada]]<ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2008 – Premier's Discovery Award <ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2010 – Elected to the [[Royal Society]]<ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2012 – Khorana Prize, [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]<ref name="UofTBio"/>
* 2017 – Inducted as an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]]<ref name="OC">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en|title=The Governor General of Canada|first=Office of the Secretary to the Governor|last=General|website=The Governor General of Canada}}</ref>
* 2017 – [[Gairdner Foundation International Award]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.utoronto.ca/news/u-t-s-lewis-e-kay-named-canada-gairdner-international-award-laureate |title=U of T's Lewis E. Kay named Canada Gairdner International Award Laureate |work=University of Toronto }}</ref>
* 2018 – [[Gerhard Herzberg Canada Gold Medal for Science and Engineering|Herzberg Medal]] of the [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada]]
* 2019 – [[Doctor of Science]] [[Honorary degree|''honoris causa'']] from The University of British Columbia <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://graduation.ok.ubc.ca/event/honorary-degrees/2019-honorary-degree-recipients/|title=2019 Honorary Degree Recipients &#124; Okanagan Graduation|website=graduation.ok.ubc.ca}}</ref>
* 2019 – [[Nakanishi Prize]]
* 2026 – Companion of the Order of Canada.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/appointments-order-canada-june-2026|title=Order of Canada Appointees – June 26, 2026}}</ref>
* 2026 – [[Royal Medal]] of the Royal Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/08/medals-and-awards-recipients-2026/|title=The Royal Society announces the medals and awards recipients 2026|publisher=Royal Society|date=27 August 2026|access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>
